description: The backup flow at the moment it is about to be abandoned. A modal titled 'Create', subtitled 'Step 4 of 5', sits over a blurred-out app window, with a grey X close button in its top-right corner. Inside, a checklist shows 'Verify you own this Trezor' completed (green tick) and step 2, 'Create shares on Trezor  10 min', active: 'Select the total number of shares, then choose the minimum number required to recover your Trezor. Example: 5 total shares, any 3 required to recover your wallet.' Three advice cards sit below it (get pen & paper or wallet backup cards / don't photograph your backup / make sure nobody is watching). A separate 'Confirm on Trezor' pill floats above the modal. The wording 'shares' is the only on-screen indication of which backup flow this is -- the page behind is blurred and unreadable.
note: Frame extracted at ffmpeg fps=4, frame 1 (~t=0s) of the original ~4.6s QuickTime screen recording attached to the reporter's follow-up comment (source recording not shipped -- no video tooling is installed on the sandbox host, so it could never be decoded by an agent).

description: The bug itself. Settings, with the 'Device' tab selected (tabs: Application, Device, Networks, Connected apps, Debug). The first section, 'Wallet backup', contains exactly ONE row -- 'Check wallet backup' ('Perform a simulated recovery to verify your wallet backup.') with a green 'Check wallet backup' button and a 'Learn more' link. Nothing else appears under that heading: the section jumps straight to 'Passphrase', then 'Firmware'. The sidebar reads 'Trezor Safe 5 / Connected', and the Firmware section shows version '2.12.2 (up to date)' and type 'Universal' -- so the device model and firmware are legible from this frame alone. What makes this the bug is a MISSING row: the multi-share backup entry that should also sit under 'Wallet backup' is absent, which a reader can only notice by knowing a second row belongs there.
note: Frame extracted at ffmpeg fps=4, frame 19 (~t=4.5s, latter half of the clip) of the original ~4.6s QuickTime screen recording (source recording not shipped -- no video tooling is installed on the sandbox host, so it could never be decoded by an agent).
